nodes.summary: For $n \ge 1$, if a polynomial $q$ of degree at most $n$ satisfies $|f - q| \le E$ on $[-1, 1]$, then the Chebyshev interpolant satisfies $|f - p_n| \le (2 + \frac{2}{\pi}\log(n + 1))E$ there. Taking $q$ the best approximation, Chebyshev interpolation loses at most a logarithmic factor against the best possible polynomial.
nodes.title: Chebyshev interpolants are near-best

nodes.summary: For $\rho > 1$, the open Bernstein ellipse $E_\rho = \{z \in \mathbb{C} : |z - 1| + |z + 1| < \rho + \rho^{-1}\}$ is the open region bounded by the ellipse with foci $\pm 1$ and semi-axis sum $\rho$; it is the image of the annulus $1 < |w| < \rho$ under the Joukowsky map $w \mapsto (w + w^{-1})/2$, together with $[-1, 1]$.
nodes.title: Open Bernstein ellipse

nodes.summary: For $f : [-1, 1] \to \mathbb{C}$, $a_k = \frac{2}{\pi} \int_0^\pi f(\cos\theta)\cos(k\theta) \, d\theta$ for $k \ge 1$ and $a_0 = \frac{1}{\pi} \int_0^\pi f(\cos\theta)\, d\theta$; after the substitution $x = \cos\theta$ these are $\frac{2}{\pi}\int_{-1}^1 f(x) T_k(x) (1 - x^2)^{-1/2} dx$ (and $\frac1\pi$ for $k = 0$).
nodes.title: Chebyshev coefficients

nodes.summary: The polynomial $p_n$ of degree at most $n$ interpolating $f$ at the $n + 1$ Chebyshev points $x_j = \cos(j\pi/n)$, $0 \le j \le n$.
nodes.title: Chebyshev interpolant

nodes.summary: The degree-$n$ truncation $f_n(x) = \sum_{k=0}^n a_k T_k(x)$ of the Chebyshev series of $f$.
nodes.title: Chebyshev projection

nodes.summary: If $f$ is continuous on $[a, b]$ with $a < b$, there is a polynomial $p$ of degree at most $n$ such that $f - p$ equioscillates, with amplitude $\max_{[a,b]}|f - p|$, at $n + 2$ points $a \le x_0 < \dots < x_{n+1} \le b$. By the proved sufficiency and uniqueness halves this $p$ is the unique best uniform approximation.
nodes.title: Existence and equioscillation of the best approximation

nodes.summary: If $f$ is Lipschitz continuous on $[-1, 1]$, then $\sum_k |a_k| < \infty$ and $f(x) = \sum_{k \ge 0} a_k T_k(x)$ for every $x \in [-1, 1]$: the Chebyshev series converges absolutely and uniformly to $f$.
nodes.title: Chebyshev series of Lipschitz functions

nodes.summary: Let $\rho > 1$ and let $f$ be analytic in the open Bernstein ellipse $E_\rho$ with $|f(z)| \le M$ there. Then $|a_0| \le M$ and $|a_k| \le 2M\rho^{-k}$ for every $k \ge 1$.
nodes.title: Chebyshev coefficients of analytic functions

nodes.summary: Under the hypotheses of Theorem 8.1, the Chebyshev interpolant satisfies $|f(x) - p_n(x)| \le 4M\rho^{-n}/(\rho - 1)$ for every $x \in [-1, 1]$ (recorded for $n \ge 1$). Geometric convergence at the rate $\rho^{-n}$ set by the largest Bernstein ellipse of analyticity is the central fact of Chebyshev technology (Chebfun).
nodes.title: Convergence of Chebyshev interpolants for analytic functions

nodes.summary: Under the hypotheses of Theorem 8.1, $|f(x) - f_n(x)| \le 2M\rho^{-n}/(\rho - 1)$ for every $x \in [-1, 1]$ and $n \ge 0$.
nodes.title: Convergence of Chebyshev projections for analytic functions

nodes.summary: For $n \ge 1$ the Lagrange basis polynomials $\ell_j$ of the $n + 1$ Chebyshev points satisfy $\sum_j |\ell_j(x)| \le \frac{2}{\pi}\log(n + 1) + 1$ for every $x \in [-1, 1]$; the Lebesgue constant grows only logarithmically (for equispaced points it grows like $2^n$).
nodes.title: Lebesgue constants of Chebyshev points

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
